verdict.reasoning: Patient reports diarrhea for 3 days and vomiting with feverishness: 'It was three days ago.' and 'I've just been... having this serious diarrhoea' and 'Yes, I've been throwing up.' and 'Yes, I've been running a serious temperature. I'm literally boiling.'

Patient describes stool as initially watery then very loose with at least 4 bowel movements today: 'It's, it's, it's very loose but it started as being very watery.' and 'Today alone, I've been at least four time.'

Patient cannot keep food or fluids down and last vomited ~2 hours ago after breakfast: 'I can't seem to be able to keep anything in me. Not even water, not even my tea, not even any liquid stuff. I've just been throwing up everything.' and 'I was sick just after trying, uh, trying to have breakfast this morning, so maybe about two hours ago.'

Pain is periumbilical, very sore, intermittent and associated with urge to defecate: 'it's kind of like towards my navel area, like I can't touch my navel area. It's just so sore. And it gets, yeah, it's almost like the center of my navel.' and 'Yes, it does come. When it comes, I feel this strong urge to go to the, to the loo.' The term 'crampy' is a reasonable clinical characterization of intermittent pain with urge to stool.

Urination is ongoing, last about 1 hour ago, with no blood in urine: 'Yeah, I've been, I've been, yeah, urinating OK.' and 'an hour ago.' in response to last urine, and 'And any blood in the stool or in the urine that you've noticed?' / 'No blood.'

Brother has similar illness and mentions others at school are affected: 'my brother, um, has actually been having similar symptoms, um, for the past, um, few days as well, and he does say like everyone in school's got this.'
Patient denies rash: 'Have you had any other symptoms at the moment, like rash?' / 'No, no rash, no, nothing that, um.'

Baseline bowel habit is once daily and normal with no prior similar episodes: 'my bowels is normally fine. I would normally go to the toilet every day. You know, in the morning, just once, yeah, and that's fine.' and 'Any episodes of diarrhoea or constipation normally?' / 'No.'

Takes daily vitamin D and ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps (dysmenorrhea): 'Well, I, I take my, my vitamins, vitamin D, every day.' and 'for my menstrual cramps, when they come, maybe I might take a, a, an ibuprofen just to ease the pain.'

Works as a graphics designer and worked from home due to illness: 'A graphics designer.' and 'I've had to actually work from home today. I'm working from home today because I can't, I can't be out for work.'
'I live with my brother and my mum.' directly supports this.
Non-smoker, occasional alcohol, no drugs: 'Well, I don't smoke, but, you know, I have a pint from time to time.' and 'And do you take any other drugs?' / 'No. Like I said, I only take, um, vitamins.'

Doctor assesses likely infectious gastroenteritis: 'it sounds like it might be some, an infectious gastroenteritis that you've got, which is usually caused by a virus. But, it can be from something you've eaten, as well.' This is effectively a working diagnosis of acute infectious gastroenteritis.
Doctor notes dehydration risk due to not keeping fluids down: 'if you're, if you're not keeping fluid down, then you can get dehydrated.' and discussion about checking hydration.

Periumbilical crampy pain is a clinical summary of 'towards my navel area... almost like the center of my navel' and intermittent pain with urge to defecate, which is consistent with crampy periumbilical pain.

Plan for urgent clinic appointment for hydration assessment and stool sample: 'I think it's probably important to get a sample of the stool' and 'we should see you so that we can check your hydration and, um, get that sample sent off as soon as possible.' and 'we can make you an urgent appointment, um, and then you can, you can get the sample sent off and we can check your hydration.'

Continue ORS in tiny frequent sips: 'you need to carry on with your rehydration salts, and just have very small amounts.' and later 'If you keep drinking, keep going with the rehydration salts. Just tiny sips constantly... just tiny, tiny sips but just keep going with it.'

Simple bland diet avoiding milk, fruit, vegetables: 'just have very simple food, if you're gonna have anything, like toast or biscuit or something really light like that. Avoid, um, fruit, vegetables, uh, milk, anything like that, which might just make it worse.'

Safety net to attend A&E if worse/unable to keep fluids down: 'but if, in the meantime, you're feeling more unwell, then we would get you seen urgently in A and E.' and patient query about not keeping water down precedes this safety-netting.
Booking via support line, agreed by patient: 'So you'll have to book an appointment through the support line.' / Patient: 'Yes, please.' / Doctor: 'Right, OK. We'll do that for you.'
